edges.description: Mutant RagC keeps mTORC1 partly active when amino acids are withdrawn.
Mutant RagC binds TFEB more strongly, independently of mTOR activity, keeping TFEB in the cytosol.
Cortical and midline brain malformations accompany the cardiac disease; the cellular route from RagC gain of function to these malformations has not been studied.
Liver dysfunction is reported with the variants; whether it is a primary hepatocyte effect or congestive hepatopathy from heart failure is not established.
No lens study of RRAGC variants exists; the link is the clinical association.
Mineral disturbance reported in one patient; mechanism unknown.
Mineral disturbance reported in one patient; mechanism unknown.
Increased cell size accompanies mTORC1 activation, but in cardiomyocytes mTOR inhibition did not normalize cell size, so this branch is contested.
Loss of nuclear TFEB lowers expression of its lysosomal and autophagy target genes.
Restoring TFEB normalizes the enlarged size of mutant cardiomyocytes.
Restoring nuclear TFEB and autophagic flux rescues cardiac function in the fish model, placing this defect upstream of the cardiomyopathy.
Hypoperfusion during cardiogenic shock; secondary mitochondrial dysfunction is also proposed.
Reduced ejection fraction, ventricular remodeling and reduced survival in adult fish.
edges.limitations: Phenotype is assessed in adult fish over months, not as a fetal or neonatal cardiomyopathy, and the zebrafish heart differs in structure and regenerative capacity. Brain, liver and lens features were not reported.

edges.description: Downregulated TFEB-controlled lysosomal genes, reduced LC3-II and glycogen deposition in mutant hearts.

nodes.description: Malformations of cortical development (pachygyria, polymicrogyria, including bilateral frontoparietal polymicrogyria) and septo-optic dysplasia. nodes.description: mTORC1 remains partly active and lysosome-associated after amino-acid withdrawal, with increased p70S6K and S6 phosphorylation.
